about: What a mod author must know before building, each question tied to the facts that answer it. known: every fact behind it is verified. partly: some of it is. open: not known; find_out says how. Checked by tests/test_gaps.py; listed by `python -m lab404 gaps`.

questions.ask: How large may an APP1 file be?
questions.why: A longer file is written past what the loader erased.

questions.ask: Does the loader check APP1 before starting it?
questions.why: Decides whether a changed APP1 can be refused at boot.

questions.ask: Can a broken APP1 lock the user out of the update screen?
questions.why: This is the way back after every failed mod.

questions.ask: What drives the pin that selects the update screen?
questions.why: If it is the second processor, the way back depends on its loader.
questions.find_out: One session on a unit saw the pin low throughout. Sample it in the first moments of APP1, find who configures pad GPIO_AD_B0_02 in APP1 and the loader, or trace the board.

questions.ask: Which files on a card can brick a unit?
questions.why: A package is copied to a card by a user who trusts it.

questions.ask: Which code inside APP1 can erase the loader?
questions.why: A hook or call there bricks a unit.

questions.ask: Is there a way back when the loader itself is erased?
questions.why: Says how bad the worst case is.
questions.find_out: The registers say the ROM falls back to its Serial Downloader. Find out, without erasing anything, whether the processor USB port reaches the connector: trace the hub, or look for the boot mode pins on the board and enter the downloader with them.

questions.ask: Can a damaged APP0 be recovered?
questions.why: Why no mod touches the second processor.
questions.find_out: Needs a read of the second processor flash with a programmer; nothing a mod can read.

questions.ask: Does anything reset a hung unit?
questions.why: Decides whether a mod needs its own fault handling.

questions.ask: Is a written APP1 verified?
questions.why: An unnoticed bad write looks like a bug in the mod.

questions.ask: Where can a mod put its code and data, and how much?
questions.why: Every mod needs room that nothing else uses.

questions.ask: How much flash is left after the image?
questions.why: Pictures and tables go there.

questions.ask: Is there free room in the fast memories (ITCM, DTCM, OCRAM)?
questions.why: Audio code in SDRAM is slower when it falls out of the cache.
questions.find_out: Map every reference into those ranges on each base; the audio DMA banks are known to live there.

questions.ask: How big is the stock heap and how full is it in use?
questions.why: A mod that allocates can starve stock code.

questions.ask: Is the free SDRAM also free on DOOM OS?
questions.why: The same address must be safe on every base a mod declares.
questions.find_out: No direct reference was found; run-time use has only been watched on the emulator. Fill the range with a pattern in a test build and check it after a long session on a unit.

questions.ask: Does memory survive a reset?
questions.why: A crash record kept in RAM depends on it.
questions.find_out: Write a marker, reset from a mod, read it back; on a unit only.

questions.ask: How much stack does each task have left?
questions.why: A hook runs on the stack of whatever called it.
questions.find_out: Stack sizes of the named tasks are known, their use is not. Fill stacks with a pattern in a test build and read the low-water mark on a unit.

questions.ask: How long is one audio block?
questions.why: Everything in the audio path must fit in it.

questions.ask: How much of a block does stock leave free?
questions.why: Says how heavy an effect may be.
questions.find_out: One measurement on one unit exists. Measure with the cycle counter on stock with many voices and effects, on more than one unit.

questions.ask: What may run in the audio, draw, file and interrupt contexts?
questions.why: The wrong work in the wrong place hung real units.
questions.find_out: The audio and interrupt rules are from bytes. The draw, file and lock rules come from failures on one unit and are not proven as rules.

questions.ask: Is floating point safe in a hook?
questions.why: Filters want it.
questions.find_out: Safe in the audio task by its attribute; other tasks and interrupts are not checked.

questions.ask: How much LED traffic can the shared serial line take?
questions.why: Lights share the line with effect parameters.
questions.find_out: The cost per message is computed, the effect on a unit under load is not measured.

questions.ask: Is a key or chord free on a screen?
questions.why: A mod must not take an input the user already has.
questions.find_out: No screen is marked complete, so `check-keys` never answers free. Finish the sweep of each screen on stock and on DOOM OS 0.7.3.

questions.ask: How does a mod open and draw a screen?
questions.why: Most functions need one.

questions.ask: How are buttons, pads and knobs read?
questions.why: Needed to add an input without losing events.

questions.ask: Where can a mod keep settings?
questions.why: Settings must survive power off and travel with a project.

questions.ask: Is a save safe against power loss?
questions.why: A half-written file loses a user's work.
questions.find_out: Stock writes its project file in place. Cut power during a save on the emulator with a drive image, then on a unit.

questions.ask: Do a mod's files follow a project on copy and export?
questions.why: Users move projects between slots and cards.

questions.ask: How are the built-in effects controlled?
questions.why: A mod can drive them without touching APP0.

questions.ask: Can a mod add an effect on the second processor?
questions.why: An original DSP program ran in the reference model. Its selection and execution on the SP remain open.
questions.find_out: Validate SP ARM plaintext with a compatible key or reference data, then trace the effect selector and DSP loader. Verify BMC update acceptance and recovery before any persistent write.

questions.ask: Which list does FX SETTING use to offer effects for BUS 3 and BUS 4?
questions.why: A type added to the MFX grid is not offered there, so a mod that adds an effect for every bus must change that list too.
questions.find_out: The list and its reader are known. Still to see: a type added this way, chosen for BUS 3 or 4 on a unit.

questions.ask: How does a mod show a crash?
questions.why: Without it every fault is a frozen unit and a guess.
questions.find_out: A private mod has a fault screen that worked on a unit once (st.import.malloc-unchecked). Make it a public example and prove it on stock.

questions.ask: Is there a way to get data out of a running unit?
questions.why: Measuring on a unit beats guessing from the stand.
questions.find_out: Files on the SD card work. The USB serial link (hw.usb.link) gives a computer a file API to both drives and a status poll without any mod; a mod writing a log to B: and a computer reading it over that link was not tried. Try that first.

questions.ask: What does a pass on the stand prove?
questions.why: So nobody calls a candidate fixed.

questions.ask: What does the second processor send back to APP1 on SAI1 receive?
questions.why: An output level meter or a recording of a bus reads it. A mod meter already uses slots 1-2 (hk.recipe.output-meter); what the stock does with it is not known.
questions.find_out: Find the stock readers of 0x20008000-0x20008FFF (watchpoint on the emulator during RESAMPLE), compare slots 1-2 with a RESAMPLE recording bit for bit, and find what slots 3-4 are.

questions.ask: Where does the stock decide how many knob cells an effect shows?
questions.why: Hiding a parameter, such as COMPRESSOR 2 MODE, needs it.
questions.find_out: The group table 0x8022E1C8 does not decide it. Trace the effect screen and the EFX SET draw on the emulator for COMPRESSOR 2 against Compressor, which has five cells.
